claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a ductile FCC matrix.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy contains B2 precipitates.
The as-cast alloy is disordered or has a low degree of chemical order.
Aging near 600°C produces L12-ordered regions in the FCC matrix whose chemistry approaches Ni3Al stoichiometry.
An L12 order parameter of approximately 0.85 corresponds to the brittle window.
Near-stoichiometric L12 ordering at approximately 600°C maximizes the antiphase boundary energy.
The B2/FCC interfaces develop a jagged or serrated morphology near 600°C.
Anisotropic growth of ordered domains causes the jagged B2/FCC interface morphology.
High antiphase boundary energy restricts dislocation cross-slip.
Restricted cross-slip forces deformation to occur through planar slip bands.
Serrations at B2/FCC interfaces concentrate stress.
The combination of planar slip and stress concentration at serrated interfaces causes brittle fracture near 600°C.
At approximately 750°C, thermal energy exceeding the ordering enthalpy reduces the L12 order parameter.
A reduction in the L12 order parameter lowers the antiphase boundary energy.
At approximately 750°C, jagged B2/FCC interfaces coarsen or become smoother.
Lower antiphase boundary energy and smoother interfaces restore cross-slip and ductility.
The ductile transition occurs when the L12 order parameter drops below approximately 0.75.
A reduction in B2/FCC interface-jaggedness amplitude by more than 50% marks the ductile transition.
The elongation after aging at 600°C is predicted to be below 5%.
The elongation after aging at 750°C is predicted to recover above 15%.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis identifies η≈0.85 as the critical order parameter corresponding to the brittle window, whereas the boundary field identifies η≈0.75 as the transition threshold. These may delimit a range, but the text presents both as the critical boundary without explaining their relationship.
